title: DC-area forecast: Flood watch issued for downpours into evening
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Scattered showers and downpours this evening. Western half of DC, southern Montgomery County near the Beltway, and eastern Fairfax County is under a flash flood warning until 7:45 p.m. A flood watch is in effect for much of the region until midnight.

What’s next? A disturbed weather pattern keeps a daily chance for at least a few showers and storms going much of the week. Highs in the mid- to upper 80s Monday and Tuesday trend hotter mid- to late week. 

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Scattered showers and a few flooding downpours roam the region this evening. An isolated storm could possess strong winds. Some spots end up with more than 1 to 2 inches of rain for the day and night. As rain takes a lull after midnight, some patchy fog may develop. Sultry lows only settle in the upper 60s to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Monday): Muggy, fairly cloudy, with rain intensity reduced. While a couple downpours and a strong storm is possible--especially midafternoon into evening--there’s a lower flooding risk. Highs in the mid- to upper 80s. Periodic showers are possible almost anytime, as a frontal boundary crosses the region. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Evening showers and storms wind down overnight, but it stays mostly cloudy. Slowly it gets less humid but lows remain in the warm 60s to near 70. Confidence: Medium

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

A slight break in the humidity may be noticeable on Tuesday with highs again in the mid- to upper 80s under partly sunny skies. Still a chance for some late-day showers and storms, but maybe not quite as many as late Monday. Confidence: Medium

Humidity ramps back up Wednesday and Thursday (it is August after all) with warmer highs in the upper 80s to low 90s. Pop-up shower and storm chances continue — be watchful of those growing cloud tops. Confidence: Low 

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: A bit blah with clouds, a muggy breeze, and a rising chance for some showers and storms. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for August 2

A tropical system in 1944 unleashed a record 6.14 inches of rain, flooding homes and streets but also providing much-needed relief from drought.
